_doc: Point-in-time retrospective. Every input was public on as_of; see sources. Hindsight lives only in outcome.json.
methodology: house v2 (EPP-distance adjustment), 6-section format; retro method r2: scenario inputs derived from dated facts by frozen rules (retro/README.md); integrated oil and gas signals

pit_profile.why: ExxonMobil: 'Their principal business is energy, involving exploration for, and production of, crude oil and natural gas, manufacture of petroleum products and transportation and sale of crude oil, natural gas and petroleum products'; 'The oil and gas business is fundamentally a commodity business. This means the operations and earnings of the Corporation and its affiliates throughout the world may be significantly affected by changes in oil, gas and petrochemical prices and by changes in margins on gasoline and other refined products'; 'The energy and petrochemical industries are highly competitive'; among the factors it lists, 'the competitiveness of alternative hydrocarbon or other energy sources' and 'laws and regulations related to environmental or energy security matters, including those addressing alternative energy sources and the risks of global climate change' (its own FY2008 10-K): earnings that move with the commodity cycle, by the company's own account; no disruption theme is live for an oil and gas producer, so the alternative-energy and climate-change wording stays here

classification.quality_note: ExxonMobil: 'Their principal business is energy, involving exploration for, and production of, crude oil and natural gas, manufacture of petroleum products and transportation and sale of crude oil, natural gas and petroleum products'; 'The oil and gas business is fundamentally a commodity business. This means the operations and earnings of the Corporation and its affiliates throughout the world may be significantly affected by changes in oil, gas and petrochemical prices and by changes in margins on gasoline and other refined products'; 'The energy and petrochemical industries are highly competitive'; among the factors it lists, 'the competitiveness of alternative hydrocarbon or other energy sources' and 'laws and regulations related to environmental or energy security matters, including those addressing alternative energy sources and the risks of global climate change' (its own FY2008 10-K): earnings that move with the commodity cycle, by the company's own account; no disruption theme is live for an oil and gas producer, so the alternative-energy and climate-change wording stays here. cyclical (obsolescence risk 2/5); price cheap; Ratio B 0.14x; -16% to EPP floor; model-vs-market gap +0.38; conservative 2yr +50%.

BEAR.desc: EPS -24.9%/yr (worst year FY99-FY08, capped at 0%); P/E to its 10th pct

BASE.desc: EPS +-36.9%/yr (Q3 revenue + margin + buyback); P/E at its 10-yr median

BULL.desc: EPS +24.4%/yr (FY99-FY08 CAGR); P/E holds its 75th pct

XBULL.desc: EPS +53.3%/yr (best 2-yr run FY99-FY08); P/E at its 90th pct

summary: XOM (retrospective, 2010-01-29) ◉ BUY — Ratio B 0.14x (34.8% downside to Bear $42 / +243.0% upside to Bull $221) | Adj composite 2.40 vs market 2.02: gap +0.38 [MODESTLY UNDERVALUED] | -15% above the EPP floor $76 (9x FY09E $8.47) | Conservative 2-yr case: +50.0% total (+25.0%/yr) | At 7.6x FY09E the 15% hurdle price $85 sits between the BASE and BULL cases; oil-equivalent production +2.7% in Q3 2009, forward revenues -40.3% (no Q4 2009 revenue guide, Q3 2009 revenue as reported); no disruption theme has dated evidence.
